newsitem.title: USA: Illinois corn plantings proceeding at record pace.
newsitem.headline: Illinois corn plantings proceeding at record pace.

text.p: Illinois corn plantings proceeded at a record pace in the week ended Sunday despite wet soils that prevented seedings in the southern district, the Illinois Agricultural Statistics Service said.
Corn was 37 percent planted as of Sunday, compared with 27 percent last year and the five-year average of 15 percent.

"Wet soils in the southern districts allowed virtually no planting, but over 50 percent of the corn in the central and east districts was planted during the week and over 20 percent of the corn in the west and west-southwest," the report said.
Some farmers had begun planting soybeans but the report did not list a percentage of the crop seeded.
Winter wheat was rated two percent very poor, four percent poor, 22 percent fair, 62 percent good and 10 percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture was rated eight percent short, 74 percent adequate and 18 percent surplus.
Pasture was rated two percent very poor, four percent poor, 32 percent fair, 54 percent good and eight percent excellent.
